name: Italian Game
description: A classical opening focused on quick development, rapid castling, and targeting the vulnerable f7 square.

variations.name: Giuoco Pianissimo (Quiet Game)
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d3 Nf6 5. c3 d6 6. O-O O-O 7. h3 a6 8. Bb3 Ba7

explanations.e4: White controls the center and opens diagonal lines.
explanations.Nf3: White develops the knight and attacks e5.
explanations.Nc6: Black protects the e5-pawn with the knight.
explanations.Bc4: White aims the bishop at the fragile f7 square.
explanations.Bc5: Black develops the bishop to an active central diagonal.
explanations.d3: White solidifies the e4-pawn for a calm, strategic build-up.
explanations.Nf6: Black develops the knight toward the center.
explanations.c3: White prepares a future d4 push and gives the bishop a retreat square.
explanations.d6: Black supports e5 and opens a path for the light-squared bishop.
explanations.O-O: White tucks the king away into safety.
Black castles safely on the kingside.
explanations.h3: White prevents Black's pieces from invading g4.
explanations.a6: Black prepares a b5 expansion and secures a retreat for the bishop.
explanations.Bb3: White safely tucks the bishop back along the diagonal.
explanations.Ba7: Black preserves the active bishop from central trades.

variations.name: Giuoco Piano (Center Center Center)
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Bd2 Bxd2+ 8. Nbxd2 d5 9. exd5 Nxd5 10. Qb3 Na5

explanations.e4: Control the center and open lines for your pieces.
explanations.Nf3: Develop your knight and attack e5.
explanations.Nc6: Black develops and protects the e5 pawn.
explanations.Bc4: Develop your bishop toward the vulnerable f7 square.
explanations.Bc5: Black develops the bishop and mirrors your setup.
explanations.c3: Prepare to build a strong pawn center with d4.
explanations.Nf6: Black develops and attacks your e4 pawn.
explanations.d4: Establish a strong central pawn presence.
explanations.cxd4: Recapture to build a full pawn duo in the center.
explanations.Bb4+: Black checks the king to gain tempo.
explanations.Bd2: White blocks the check and offers a bishop trade.
explanations.Bxd2+: Black exchanges bishops to neutralize White's initiative.
explanations.Nbxd2: White recaptures with the knight, continuing development.
explanations.d5: Black strikes back in the center to break White's pawn duo.
explanations.exd5: White takes the pawn to open central files.
explanations.Nxd5: Black recaptures with the knight in the center.
explanations.Qb3: White places the queen on a double threat targeting d5 and b7.
explanations.Na5: Black counterattacks White's queen to defend.

variations.name: Two Knights Defense – Modern Line
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d3 Bc5 5. c3 d6 6. O-O a6 7. a4 Ba7 8. Re1 O-O

explanations.Nc6: Black defends with the queen's knight.
explanations.Bc4: White aims the Italian bishop at f7.
explanations.Nf6: Black counterattacks White's e4-pawn (Two Knights setup).
explanations.d3: White solidifies e4 and chooses a solid positional approach.
explanations.Bc5: Black transposes to a harmonious Giuoco Piano setup.
explanations.c3: White controls d4 and prepares a potential central expansion.
explanations.d6: Black reinforces e5 and opens lines for the light-squared bishop.
explanations.a6: Black creates a safe retreat square on a7 for the bishop.
explanations.a4: White halts Black's b5 expansion plans.
explanations.Ba7: Black safely moves the bishop out of potential central clashes.
explanations.Re1: White activates the rook along the central e-file.

variations.name: Fried Liver Attack (Fegatello)
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Nxd5 6. Nxf7 Kxf7 7. Qf3+ Ke6 8. Nc3 Ne7 9. d4 c6

explanations.Nf6: Black invites tactical complexity with Two Knights Defense.
explanations.Ng5: White launches an immediate tactical assault on f7.
explanations.d5: Black blocks the bishop's line of attack.
explanations.exd5: White opens the file by capturing the pawn.
explanations.Nxd5: Black recaptures, walking directly into the sacrifice.
explanations.Nxf7: White sacrifices the knight to drag Black's king into the open!
explanations.Kxf7: Black's king is forced to take the piece.
explanations.Qf3+: White brings the queen out with a fierce check, pinning the d5-knight.
explanations.Ke6: Black's king is forced to step forward into danger to defend.
explanations.Nc3: White increases pressure on the pinned d5-knight.
explanations.Ne7: Black adds a second defender to the d5-knight.
explanations.d4: White strikes open the center to attack the exposed king.

variations.name: Traxler Counterattack
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 Bc5 5. Nxf7 Bxf2+ 6. Kxf2 Nxe4+ 7. Kg1 Qh4 8. g3 Nxg3

explanations.e4: White opens with the king's pawn.
explanations.Bc5: Black ignores the attack on f7 and counterattacks f2 (Traxler Gambit)!
explanations.Nxf7: White takes the bait on f7, attacking queen and rook.
explanations.Bxf2+: Black sacrifices the bishop on f2 to shatter White's king position!
explanations.Nxe4+: Black delivers a tactical check with the knight.
explanations.Kg1: White's king steps back into safety.
explanations.Qh4: Black threatens immediate checkmate on f2.
explanations.g3: White creates an escape square and blocks the queen.
explanations.Nxg3: Black sacrifices another piece to break open White's kingside.

variations.name: Evans Gambit Accepted
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Ba5 6. d4 exd4 7. O-O dxc3 8. Qb3 Qf6

explanations.Bc4: White sets up the Italian bishop.
explanations.Bc5: Black plays the main bishop line.
explanations.b4: White offers the Evans Gambit, sacrificing a wing pawn for full central domination!
explanations.c3: White attacks the bishop and prepares a massive d4 pawn center.
explanations.Ba5: Black retreats the bishop while maintaining pressure on c3.
explanations.O-O: White completes castling and prioritizes rapid piece deployment.
explanations.Qb3: White creates a lethal battery targeting f7 and b7.
explanations.Qf6: Black brings out the queen to guard f7.

variations.name: Deutz Gambit
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O Nf6 5. d4 Bxd4 6. Nxd4 Nxd4 7. Bg5 h6 8. Bh4 g5

explanations.O-O: White castles early to prepare a swift central break.
explanations.d4: White sacrifices the d4-pawn to open central lines rapidly.
explanations.Nxd4: White trades knights to open lines.
Black recaptures centrally with the knight.
explanations.Bg5: White pins Black's knight to create tactical counterplay.
explanations.h6: Black puts the question to the bishop.
explanations.Bh4: White retreats along the pin diagonal.
explanations.g5: Black aggressively pushes pawns to break the pin.

variations.name: Italian Gambit
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d4 exd4 5. c3 dxc3 6. Bxf7+ Kxf7 7. Qd5+ Kf8 8. Qxc5+ d6

explanations.d4: White strikes immediately in the center with a gambit.
explanations.c3: White offers a second pawn to accelerate piece activity.
explanations.Bxf7+: White strikes on f7 to strip Black's king of castling rights.
explanations.Qd5+: White checks with the queen to regain material.
explanations.Kf8: Black's king steps back into safety.
explanations.d6: Black opens lines for the remaining pieces.

variations.name: Max Lange Attack
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d4 exd4 5. O-O Bc5 6. e5 d5 7. exf6 dxc4 8. Re1+ Be6

explanations.e4: White opens with the king's pawn.
explanations.O-O: White castles to prepare a tactical onslaught down the e-file.
explanations.e5: White pushes the e-pawn to displace the knight.
explanations.d5: Black strikes back in the center, attacking White's bishop.
explanations.Re1+: White checks along the open e-file.
explanations.Be6: Black blocks the check with the bishop.

variations.name: Blackburne-Shilling Gambit Trap
variations.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nd4 4. Nxe5 Qg5 5. Nxf7 Qxg2 6. Rf1 Qxe4+ 7. Be2 Nf3#

explanations.Nd4: Black sets a dubious trap, leaving the e5-pawn undefended.
explanations.Nxe5: White falls into the trap and takes the free pawn.
explanations.Qg5: Black's queen attacks both the knight on e5 and the g2-pawn.
explanations.Nxf7: White greedily forks the queen and rook on f7.
explanations.Qxg2: Black attacks the f1-rook and threatens checkmate.
explanations.Rf1: White's rook flees to save itself.
explanations.Nf3#: Smothered mate! The knight delivers checkmate as White's king is trapped by its own pieces.
